Marvell Buys Lumentum for $115 Billion.
▪Marvell Technology Inc. agreed to pay $115 billion for Lumentum Holdings Inc., one of the largest chip deals on record.
▪The price tag has already shrunk by about a quarter as Marvell is paying entirely in its own shares, and investors have been selling them since reports of the talks surfaced.
▪Marvell management framed the deal as a race to own the shift from copper to optics inside AI data centers, with the combined company expected to rank among the five largest AI infrastructure chip companies.

Piero Cingari
11/02/2026 08:49:36 [BZG]
Benzinga Newswire

On paper, Marvell Technology Inc.(NASDAQ:MRVL) just agreed to pay $115 billion for Lumentum Holdings Inc. (NASDAQ:LITE), one of the largest chip deals on record.

In practice, the price tag has already shrunk by about a quarter.

Marvell is paying entirely in its own shares, and investors have been selling them since reports of the talks surfaced last Wednesday.

Under the official terms announced Monday, Lumentum holders will receive 4.5 Marvell shares for each share they own. That valued Lumentum at about $1,132 a share, or a 23.9% premium, based on Oct. 28 closing prices. Lumentum holders will end up with about a third of the combined company, and the deal is expected to close in the first half of 2028.

The market has since rewritten those terms.

Marvell has dropped 25% from its Oct. 28 close, shedding roughly $55 billion in market value, as investors balked at the price and the dilution.

The stock fell another 4.5% to $187.39 in early Monday trading.

Because the deal is paid entirely in stock, Marvell’s slide has also reduced the offer’s value.

The 4.5 Marvell shares promised for each Lumentum share were worth about $1,132 when the terms were set. At Monday’s premarket price, they are worth about $849, a quarter less.

Management framed the deal as a race to own the shift from copper to optics inside AI data centers.

“AI infrastructure is undergoing a fundamental architectural shift toward optical connectivity, creating an opportunity that comes along once in a generation,” Marvell Chairman and CEO Matt Murphy said.

“The companies that move first and help define this transition will set the standard for decades to come,” he added.

On a joint call with analysts, Murphy said he expects the combined group to rank among the five largest AI infrastructure chip companies.

Lumentum CEO Michael Hurlston, who will join Marvell’s board, pointed to the size of the prize.

“Joining Marvell creates a company uniquely positioned to capitalize on a market opportunity of $550 billion and generate significant, sustainable stockholder value,” Hurlston said.
“Surging AI data traffic requires rapid hardware innovation, and this combination enhances our ability to deliver next-generation solutions at scale,” he added.

Marvell brings interconnect, switching and custom AI chips. Lumentum adds lasers, optical transceivers, optical circuit switching and its own indium phosphide manufacturing. The companies expect more than $1 billion in annual cost synergies and a deal that adds to Marvell’s adjusted earnings in the first year after closing.

That one time I asked Seema Verma what she'd change if she were back at CMS…

Recently, I sat down with Seema Verma, EVP and GM of Oracle Health and Life Sciences and former CMS Administrator, to talk about Oracle's agentic AI future. Full link below, but sharing 5 great takeaways/quotes here:

1. On regulating at the speed of AI

AI is “going to change the way we work. So some things CMS requires today may not be reasonable anymore,” Verma said.

“Take rev cycle and coding. The reason we have coding is that we used to be on a paper system. The doctor would write their notes, and we needed a way to translate what happened in that interaction into a set of codes tied to reimbursement. With AI and ambient listening, it's possible to take the recording of the encounter and completely transact the payment from it. Maybe we don't even need coding going forward. But CMS ties everything to coding. So even when AI is capable of transacting, issuing the payment, and doing the prior authorization, the system still requires it.”

2. On walled gardens

From her CMS days: “When I was administrator, I heard from a lot of innovators who were very frustrated. It was hard for them to do business and bring innovative solutions to the marketplace, because it seemed like there was always a walled garden, or a front door they had to go through.”

Her view: customers should make the decisions about innovation and what products they use because it's their system and their patients.

3. On a system of record meeting a system of intelligence

Verma’s argument is that AI hallucinates when it lacks real-time data, and legacy EHRs weren't built to provide it. “You need a system that can access enterprise data - not just what's in the EHR, but what's in your supply chain, your financial systems, human resources."

4. On Oracle differentiating itself

“What's differentiating is that this EHR has been built from the ground up for AI. It's also being built with safety in mind, so we've layered in monitoring, transparency, and human in the loop. It's built for the future era.”

5. On keeping a thriving innovation ecosystem while also building AI-native products themselves

“It's an open ecosystem, an open platform. We're going to build the base product: the EHR, the patient portal, rev cycle. But because it sits on a platform, customers can say, ‘You know what, I actually want to build this one myself,’ or ‘I like this product from another vendor,’ and build it right into their ecosystem... We want to drive better outcomes, and if a competitor's product does that, we would certainly not want to prevent our customers from using best-of-breed solutions.”

De Raad van State is bijzonder kritisch over de nieuwe box 3-plannen.

Het advies is duidelijk: trek het huidige wetsvoorstel in en kom met een nieuw stelsel dat in 2030 ingaat.

En daarmee worden meteen een paar problemen opgelost!

Het was namelijk al de bedoeling om vanaf 2030 ook goud en bitcoin onder de vermogenswinstbelasting te brengen. 

Als het kabinet het advies van de Raad van State volgt en in 2030 in één keer overstapt op een nieuw stelsel, verdwijnt ook het probleem van de tijdelijke ongelijke behandeling tussen vermogensaanwas- en vermogenswinstbelasting.

Daarmee verdwijnt bovendien een belangrijke aanleiding voor nieuwe rechtszaken.
En dan zijn ook die 252 extra fte die de Belastingdienst tijdelijk nodig zou hebben voor de voorgestelde wijzigingen niet meer nodig. 

Mooi, want het kabinet heeft voor de zoveelste keer beloofd de overheid nu écht kleiner te maken. Overigens waren er voor de nieuwe box 3-plannen al 900 extra fte voorzien.

Dus we moeten niet te snel conclusies trekken. En al helemaal niet stoppen met beleggen vanwege de onzekerheid rond box 3.

Dat neemt niet weg dat een aantal fundamentele problemen gewoon blijft bestaan. Zoals het exorbitant hoge belastingtarief van 36% en het feit dat inflatie niet wordt gecompenseerd. Je betaalt dus ook belasting over rendement dat je koopkracht helemaal niet vergroot.  Daar schreef ik eerder al een artikel over.

De Raad van State heeft bovendien een belangrijk punt: waarom met zoveel haast een ingewikkeld belastingstelsel invoeren als zelfs de Belastingdienst aangeeft dat het niet uitvoerbaar is?

Terug naar de tekentafel is dan ook een goed idee. We schreven op onze Substack al twee keer uitgebreid over box 3 en de gevolgen voor beleggers.
